name: ScrollingFrame
simple: A ScrollingFrame is a Frame that can hold more stuff than fits inside it, and lets the player scroll to see the rest, with a mouse wheel, a finger swipe, or the scroll bar. It's how you make inventories, shop lists and leaderboards that can be longer than the window.
analogy: A ScrollingFrame is like a window on a long scroll of paper. The window stays the same size, but you can roll the paper up and down to read all of it.
whenToUse: Long shop lists or quest lists
Chat logs or leaderboards that keep growing
where: Inside a ScreenGui, SurfaceGui or BillboardGui. Create it in Studio or with Instance.new("ScrollingFrame") in a LocalScript.

terms.UI / GUI: User Interface: the buttons, menus, text and pictures drawn on the screen or on things in the game.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.ScreenGui: The invisible container that holds UI shown on the player's screen. It must be inside the player's PlayerGui (put it in StarterGui in Studio).
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside.
terms.UDim2: The value used for Size and Position: (X Scale, X Offset, Y Scale, Y Offset). Scale is a fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size; Offset is exact pixels.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts, like Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) for red.
terms.canvas: The big 'paper' inside the ScrollingFrame that holds the content. It can be larger than the frame; the part that fits in the window is what you see.
terms.CanvasSize: How big the scrollable paper is. If the frame is 300 pixels tall and CanvasSize is 900 pixels tall, you can scroll down 600 pixels.
terms.scroll bar: The thin bar on the side you can drag to scroll.
terms.inset: Pushed in to make room. An inset canvas gets a bit smaller so the scroll bar doesn't cover content.
terms.elastic scrolling: The bouncy 'rubber band' effect on phones when you scroll past the end.
terms.inertia: When you flick a list on a phone and it keeps sliding for a bit after you let go.
terms.AutomaticSize: A setting that makes something grow to fit its content.

examples.title: A scrolling list that grows to fit its items
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local list = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
list.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(250, 300)              -- the window: 250 x 300 pixels
list.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 100)
list.CanvasSize = UDim2.fromScale(0, 0)             -- start with no extra canvas...
list.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y     -- ...and let it grow downward to fit
list.ScrollingDirection = Enum.ScrollingDirection.Y -- only scroll up and down
list.ScrollBarThickness = 8
list.Parent = screenGui

local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 5) -- 5 pixels between items
layout.Parent = list

for i = 1, 20 do
	local item = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	item.Size = UDim2.new(1, -10, 0, 40) -- full width minus 10 px, 40 px tall
	item.Text = "Item " .. i
	item.Parent = list
end
explain: The ScrollingFrame window is 300 pixels tall.
20 items x 40 pixels + 19 gaps x 5 pixels = 895 pixels of content, way more than 300.
AutomaticCanvasSize Y makes the canvas grow tall enough for all items, so you can scroll down about 595 pixels.
UIListLayout stacks the labels in a column so we don't have to position each one.

gotchas: If you can't scroll, the CanvasSize is probably not bigger than the frame. Use AutomaticCanvasSize, or set CanvasSize bigger.
CanvasSize Scale is measured against the ScrollingFrame itself. CanvasSize UDim2.fromScale(0, 2) makes the canvas twice as tall as the frame.
UICorner and UIGradient don't work on a ScrollingFrame. Put the ScrollingFrame inside a rounded Frame instead.
Children with Scale sizes are measured against the canvas, which can make them huge if the canvas is big. Offset heights are often easier inside lists.

ScrollingFrame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.simple: Read-only. The real size of the scrollable canvas in pixels, after AutomaticCanvasSize has done its work.
ScrollingFrame.AbsoluteCanvasSize.example:
local list = script.Parent
print("Canvas is", list.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y, "pixels tall")

ScrollingFrame.AbsoluteWindowSize.simple: Read-only. The size in pixels of the visible area, not counting the space taken by scroll bars. A 300-wide frame with an 8-pixel scroll bar showing gives about 292.
ScrollingFrame.AbsoluteWindowSize.example:
local list = script.Parent
print("Visible area:", list.AbsoluteWindowSize)

ScrollingFrame.AutomaticCanvasSize.simple: Makes the canvas grow automatically to fit everything inside. X = grow sideways, Y = grow downward, XY = both. Saves you from working out CanvasSize by hand.
ScrollingFrame.AutomaticCanvasSize.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.CanvasSize = UDim2.fromScale(0, 0)
list.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y

ScrollingFrame.BottomImage.simple: The picture used for the bottom end of the vertical scroll bar (or the right end of the horizontal one). Change it to give your scroll bar a custom look.
ScrollingFrame.BottomImage.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.BottomImage = "rbxassetid://1234567890" -- replace with your image ID

ScrollingFrame.BottomImageContent.simple: The newer Content version of BottomImage. Same picture, different value type. Only supports asset links.

ScrollingFrame.CanvasPosition.simple: How far the canvas is scrolled, in pixels, from the top-left. (0, 0) is the very top. Set it to jump to a spot, read it to know where the player scrolled.
ScrollingFrame.CanvasPosition.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, 0) -- jump back to the top
ScrollingFrame.CanvasPosition.gotcha: Doesn't do anything if there's nothing to scroll.

ScrollingFrame.CanvasSize.simple: How big the scrollable paper is, as a UDim2. Scale is a fraction of the ScrollingFrame's own size, Offset is pixels. On a 300-pixel-tall frame, UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 900) means 900 pixels of content, so you can scroll 600 pixels down.
ScrollingFrame.CanvasSize.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 900) -- 900 px tall canvas
ScrollingFrame.CanvasSize.gotcha: If it isn't bigger than the frame, nothing scrolls. AutomaticCanvasSize can do it for you.

ScrollingFrame.ElasticBehavior.simple: On touch screens, decides whether the list bounces when you scroll past the end. WhenScrollable (default), Always or Never.
ScrollingFrame.ElasticBehavior.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.ElasticBehavior = Enum.ElasticBehavior.Never -- no bouncing

ScrollingFrame.HorizontalScrollBarInset.simple: Whether the canvas gets shorter to make room for the horizontal (bottom) scroll bar. None (default) = the bar may cover content. ScrollBar = make room only while the bar shows. Always = always make room.

ScrollingFrame.MidImage.simple: The picture for the middle, stretchy part of the scroll bar, between TopImage and BottomImage.
ScrollingFrame.MidImage.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.MidImage = "rbxassetid://1234567890" -- replace with your image ID

ScrollingFrame.MidImageContent.simple: The newer Content version of MidImage. Only supports asset links.

ScrollingFrame.ScrollBarImageColor3.simple: Tints the scroll bar pictures with a color. White means no tint. Easy way to make the scroll bar match your theme.
ScrollingFrame.ScrollBarImageColor3.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.ScrollBarImageColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 170, 255) -- blue scroll bar

ScrollingFrame.ScrollBarImageTransparenc.simple: How see-through the scroll bar is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.

ScrollingFrame.ScrollBarThickness.simple: How thick the scroll bars are, in pixels. 0 hides them (you can still scroll with the wheel or a finger).

ScrollingFrame.ScrollingDirection.simple: Which ways the player can scroll: X (sideways), Y (up and down) or XY (both, the default).

ScrollingFrame.ScrollingEnabled.simple: Turns scrolling on or off. When false, the player can't scroll and no scroll bars show.
ScrollingFrame.ScrollingEnabled.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.ScrollingEnabled = false -- freeze the list

ScrollingFrame.TopImage.simple: The picture for the top end of the vertical scroll bar (or the left end of the horizontal one).
ScrollingFrame.TopImage.example:
local list = script.Parent
list.TopImage = "rbxassetid://1234567890" -- replace with your image ID

ScrollingFrame.TopImageContent.simple: The newer Content version of TopImage. Only supports asset links.

ScrollingFrame.VerticalScrollBarInset.simple: Whether the canvas gets narrower to make room for the vertical (side) scroll bar. None (default) = the bar may cover content. ScrollBar = make room only while the bar shows. Always = always make room.

ScrollingFrame.VerticalScrollBarPosition.simple: Puts the vertical scroll bar on the Right (default) or Left side.

ScrollingFrame:GetScrollVelocity.simple: Returns how fast (as a Vector2, in each direction) the list is still sliding after the player flicks it and lets go, mostly on touch screens.
ScrollingFrame:GetScrollVelocity.example:
local list = script.Parent
print("Still sliding at", list:GetScrollVelocity())
ScrollingFrame:GetScrollVelocity.gotcha: You'll mostly see real numbers on a phone or in Studio's Device Emulator.

ScrollingFrame:ResetScrollVelocity.simple: Stops any leftover sliding right away by setting the scroll speed to 0.
ScrollingFrame:ResetScrollVelocity.example:
local list = script.Parent
list:ResetScrollVelocity() -- stop the list from sliding
list.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, 0)
